name: Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX
provider: Defence Innovation Organisation, Ministry of Defence
summary: A larger iDEX grant for startups and innovators developing strategically critical defence technologies that need much bigger budgets. It funds up to half of a product development budget, with challenges and hackathons run against defence problem statements. Winners are incubated by iDEX Partner Incubators and must bring the remaining money themselves.
amount: Up to 50% of the product development budget, capped at ₹25 crore
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup or Indian company under the Companies Act
Individual innovators can also apply
Working on a listed critical or strategic technology challenge
howToApply: Watch the iDEX challenges page for an ADITI edition
Choose a listed problem statement
Apply online before the closing date
statusNote: ADITI 4 is listed as closed with a last date of 4 May 2026. The scheme paper budgets FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26, and no notice covering later years or another edition was found.
watchOut: You must fund the other half, which can mean raising serious money. The published budget period ended in FY 2025-26, so a further edition is not assured. This is for hard defence technology, not typical SaaS.

name: Seed Funding with Equity, Andhra Pradesh Innovation and Startup Policy 4.0
provider: Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society, ITE&C Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
summary: State equity funding for startups registered in Andhra Pradesh, on an equity sharing model. The policy lists a separate go-to-market support line of the same size, also for equity, and need-based seed funding of up to ₹1 crore for deep tech and advanced technology startups. The share of equity is not stated in the policy.
amount: Up to ₹50 lakh for equity; deep tech and advanced technology startups up to ₹1 crore based on need
eligibility: Registered with the Government of Andhra Pradesh on the AP Startup One portal
Equity sharing with the state's funding model
Deep tech and advanced technology startups for the ₹1 crore line
howToApply: Register on the AP Startup One portal
Apply through the rolling application portal
Ask the Innovation Society about current programmes such as AP Build
statusNote: APIS home page says the application portal stays open on a rolling basis. Policy valid five years from notification or until replaced. Equity terms were not seen; operating guidelines are issued separately.
watchOut: You give up equity and the policy does not say how much. Ask for the equity terms in writing, and compare them with what an angel would offer, before you accept.

name: Startup Grants, Andhra Pradesh Innovation and Startup Policy 4.0
provider: Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society, ITE&C Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
summary: Grants to turn an idea into a tested product. A startup can get an upfront amount of up to ₹2 lakh, then more in phases based on its stage and performance until the product is viable. The limit is higher for startups with a founder who is a woman, BC, SC, ST, minority or differently abled.
amount: Up to ₹15 lakh in total, or ₹20 lakh with a founder from specified groups; initial grant up to ₹2 lakh
eligibility: Registered with the Government of Andhra Pradesh on the AP Startup One portal
Working to turn an innovative idea into a tested solution or proof of concept
Further phases depend on stage and performance
₹20 lakh limit needs a founder from the listed groups
howToApply: Register on the AP Startup One portal
Read the application process for the AP Ignite programme on the APIS site
Apply on the portal, which is open on a rolling basis
statusNote: APIS home page announces the application portal stays open on a rolling basis. G.O. dated 24.03.2025 says the policy is valid five years from notification or until replaced.
watchOut: Money comes in phases, so ₹15 lakh is reached only if you keep clearing reviews. Operating guidelines are issued separately, so ask what each stage demands before you plan your spend.

name: Atal Incubation Centres
provider: Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog
summary: A network of 72 incubators backed by Atal Innovation Mission, many focused on sectors such as health, energy, agriculture, education and cyber security. Startups can join a centre for workspace, equipment, mentors, business planning, industry partnerships and help reaching seed capital. Government grants go to the centre rather than to startups directly.
eligibility: Innovative startup aiming to be scalable
Fits the focus sector of the chosen centre
Accepted through that centre's own selection
howToApply: Look up Atal Incubation Centres in India on the AIM site
Contact a centre that suits your sector
Apply through its own intake
statusNote: AIM's home page says the portals for new ATL, AIC and ACIC applications are not open. That concerns institutions setting up centres. No central founder intake is shown, and each existing centre runs its own.
watchOut: The ₹10 crore figure online is a grant to set up a centre, not money for your startup. AIM publishes no founder amount, so ask each centre about its fees, equity and any seed support.

name: AWS Activate Credits
provider: Amazon Web Services
summary: AWS credits for startups below Series B. Self-funded founders can apply directly under the Founders tier and start with $1,000, rising to $5,000 for select participants. Startups linked to an accelerator, angel or VC can apply under the Portfolio tier for up to $200,000. A further invite-only tier exists for AI startups.
amount: Up to $5,000 for self-funded startups (starts at $1,000). Up to $200,000 with an Activate Provider. $200,000+ for AI startups, invite only.
eligibility: Has not raised a Series B.
Founded in the last 10 years.
AWS account on a paid tier plan.
New to Activate Credits, or asking for more than you received before.
The Portfolio tier needs an Organization ID from your Activate Provider.
howToApply: Create or sign in with an AWS Builder ID using a professional email.
Pick Founders if self-funded, or enter your provider's Org ID for Portfolio.
Add product, funding and company details, link an AWS account, and submit.
AWS says to expect a reply in 5 to 10 business days.
statusNote: Application page live with no deadline or cohort dates shown. The page does not list any country limits.
watchOut: The headline $200,000 is not open to bootstrapped founders. Without an Activate Provider's Org ID you are capped at $5,000, and most people should plan around the first $1,000.

name: Seed Support, Bihar Startup Policy 2022
provider: Department of Industries, Government of Bihar
summary: An interest-free loan for startups recognised by the Bihar government, repayable over ten years. Money is released as the startup hits milestones. It can pay for idea validation, prototypes, market research, marketing and initial setup. Women, SC, ST and differently abled founders get extra support. Startups take an evaluation test as part of selection.
amount: Up to ₹10 lakh as an interest-free loan
eligibility: Registered on the Startup Bihar portal and recognised by the Department of Industries
Registered with an incubation centre
Startup puts in 5% of the seed amount
Extra support only where owned fully by women, SC, ST or differently abled founders
howToApply: Register on the Startup Bihar portal during an open window
Take the evaluation test
Apply for the benefit through the portal
statusNote: Startup Bihar home page shows applications were open 1 October to 31 October 2026, 11:59 PM, now closed. Evaluation test results were posted through 2026. Next window not shown.
watchOut: This is a loan, not a grant, even though some pages say seed grant. Conditions come from a Startup India summary of an older policy text, so confirm them with Startup Bihar.

name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant
provider: BIRAC, Department of Biotechnology, Government of India
summary: BIRAC's flagship early-stage grant for biotech startups turning an innovative idea into proof of concept. Selected applicants get grant money for up to 18 months, paid in stages against milestones, along with mentoring and networking through BIG Partners. It is for life sciences work and needs a functioning lab or an incubator.
amount: Up to ₹50 lakh as grant-in-aid for up to 18 months
eligibility: Company or LLP registered in India
Incorporated not more than 5 years before the call opens
At least 51% owned by resident Indian citizens or Indian-owned companies
Own working R&D facility, or incubated at an incubator
A technically qualified Project Leader

Wait for the national call, normally on 1 January and 1 July
Submit your proposal online before the system closes
Clear screening, expert review and committee stages
statusNote: BIRAC says calls are announced twice a year, on 1 January and 1 July, and stay open about 45 days. Its current calls table was empty when checked, and the site was updated 2 November 2026.
watchOut: Windows are short and the portal closes automatically at the stated time. Competition is national, and being only a biotech idea is not enough, since you need lab access. Software-only health ideas are a poor fit.

name: Cartier Women's Initiative Regional Awards
provider: Cartier Women's Initiative
summary: An annual international award for women-run impact businesses, with South Asia and Central Asia as one of nine regions. Three fellows from each region receive grants of $100,000, $60,000 or $30,000 by place, plus a fellowship with training and a network. Businesses need revenue, a team and a measurable social or environmental impact.
amount: $100,000 for first place, $60,000 for second, $30,000 for third
eligibility: Annual revenue between $50,000 and $5 million in the last closed fiscal year.
Between 5 and 250 team members, counting contractors and part-time staff.
No more than $2 million raised in equity, SAFEs or convertible notes.
A woman in a main leadership role, owning a share equal to or above each co-founder.
An incorporated for-profit business, majority owned by founders and team. Sole proprietorships and non-profits are out.
Measurable social or environmental impact tied to at least one UN Sustainable Development Goal.
howToApply: Read the application guide and scoring rubric on the Regional Awards page.
Submit one online application in English, as a founder who meets every rule, when the next edition opens.
Finalists are ranked by a jury.
statusNote: Applications for the 2027 edition are closed. That deadline was 16 June 2026, with fellows announced in spring 2027. The next edition's dates are not posted.
watchOut: Only three fellows win per large region. The revenue floor rules out pre-revenue startups, and a plain SaaS with no measurable impact will not fit. Grants may also be taxable locally.

name: Claude for Startups
provider: Anthropic
summary: A cohort programme for early-stage founders building on Claude. It offers discounts and credits worth up to $45,000 from companies building with Claude, regular Applied AI sessions, and invitations to events. Founders backed by a VC in Anthropic's partner network may also claim up to $100,000 in API credits through that VC.
amount: Partner discounts and credits worth up to $45,000. VC-backed founders may get up to $100,000 in additional API credits through their VC.
eligibility: Aimed at early-stage founders building on Claude.
The extra API credits need backing from a VC in Anthropic's partner network and are claimed through that VC.
Credits apply to the first-party Claude API through Claude Console, not AWS, Google Cloud or Azure.
howToApply: Applications are paused, so subscribe to the Claude Startup newsletter on the programme page.
Apply when the next cohort opens.
If VC-backed, ask your VC whether it can unlock the API credits.
statusNote: The page says the current cohort is full and new applications are not being accepted. It gives no date for the next cohort. No country limit is stated.
watchOut: The $45,000 is described as offers from other companies, not Anthropic API credits. The $100,000 needs a partner VC, which most bootstrapped Indian founders will not have.

name: Cloudflare for Startups
provider: Cloudflare
summary: Cloudflare credits valid for one year, sized by how much you have raised. Bootstrapped companies with under $1 million raised can get $10,000. Companies funded by an affiliated partner can get $100,000 with under $5 million raised, or $350,000 with $5 million or more. Higher tiers add technical sessions and support.
amount: $10,000, $100,000 or $350,000 by tier, valid for one year.
eligibility: Incorporated within the last 10 years.
Funded up to Series B, with funding in the last 12 months.
Actively building a technology product, with a live website and a public LinkedIn, X or GitHub presence.
First-time applicant, for-profit, using a business email on your own domain.
Consultancies, agencies, managed service providers, resellers, educational institutions and personal blogs are excluded.
howToApply: Use the Apply button on the programme page.
Reviews typically take up to 48 hours, and approval comes by email.
If you hear nothing after a week, write to startups@cloudflare.com.
statusNote: Application form linked from the page with no deadline shown. No country limit is stated.
watchOut: The two big tiers need a partner investor. Some products have sub-limits, such as R2 at $10,000 and Workers AI at $2,500 on the lowest tier. The funding rule and bootstrapped tier read awkwardly, so check first.

name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
provider: Ministry of MSME and SIDBI
summary: Lets new or existing micro and small enterprises, including service and trading businesses, borrow from banks and other lenders without collateral or a third-party guarantee. The trust guarantees a share of the loan to the lender. Cover is higher for micro loans and for women and SC or ST founders, among others.
amount: Guarantee cover up to ₹10 crore per borrower, covering 75% to 90% depending on category and loan size
eligibility: New or existing micro or small enterprise, as the MSME Ministry defines it
Loan from a lender registered with the trust
Credit given without collateral or third-party guarantee, or under the partial collateral option
howToApply: Approach a registered lender for a term loan or working capital
The lender assesses and sanctions under its own process
The lender then applies for the guarantee and pays the fee
statusNote: The CGTMSE site shows activity to 31 March 2026, with 322 registered lenders and notices on the ₹10 crore limit. The guarantee scheme document is updated to 1 April 2025. No end date or window is published.
watchOut: You cannot apply yourself, because the lender has to agree first. Guarantee fees start at 0.37% a year and rise with loan size, and lenders often pass them on. CGTMSE warns about lookalike sites and agents.

name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups
provider: DPIIT, operated by National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC)
summary: Gives banks, NBFCs and venture debt funds a government guarantee on money they lend to DPIIT-recognised startups, so they can lend with less collateral. Cover reaches 85% of the default on loans up to ₹10 crore and 75% above that. The startup still has to win and repay the loan.
amount: Guarantee cover up to ₹20 crore per borrower. This protects the lender and is not cash to you.
eligibility: Recognised by DPIIT
Not in default to any lender or investor
Not classified as a Non-Performing Asset under RBI rules
Eligibility certified by the member lender
howToApply: Get DPIIT recognition first
Apply online for the startup loan on the Jan Samarth portal, or visit a branch of a member lender
The lender appraises you under its normal rules and takes the guarantee from NCGTC
statusNote: No end date is published. The NCGTC page lists the May 2025 gazette notification and 2025-26 FAQ, and the Startup India page was last updated 30 October 2026. Jan Samarth has a live startup loan route.
watchOut: A guarantee is not a loan approval. The lender still judges your cash flows, and Jan Samarth asks for at least 25% margin plus audited balance sheets and a project report from existing units.

name: ElevenLabs Startup Grants
provider: ElevenLabs
summary: Twelve months of free access to the ElevenLabs voice AI platform for small startups, on its Scale plan. The grant includes 33 million characters, which ElevenLabs values at more than $5,500, plus founder events and startup support. It suits founders building voice agents, speech or audio features into a long-term product.
amount: 12 months of free access with 33,000,000 characters, valued by ElevenLabs at more than $5,500.
eligibility: Fewer than 25 employees when you apply.
A business or monetisation plan, and a valid business email.
A long-term product, not a one-off project or campaign.
Agencies, consulting firms and SMBs are not eligible.
One application per company. Existing enterprise customers cannot apply.
howToApply: Submit the form on the grants page, covering your startup, team and growth plans.
Reviews are rolling, with a reply expected within one week.
The grant is applied to the account you applied with.
statusNote: The page says applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with no deadline. No country limit is stated.
watchOut: This is usage on one vendor's platform, not money. After 12 months the account drops to the Free plan unless you choose to pay, so plan for that cost.

name: Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups
provider: Ministry of Electronics and IT, through MeitY Startup Hub
summary: MeitY's umbrella scheme for tech startups, focused on Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Through selected implementing agencies it offers entrepreneur-in-residence support, early-stage money, pilot funding, matched investment and a larger cheque for a few deep tech startups. Its entrepreneur-in-residence track has a third cohort call running now.
amount: Up to ₹10 lakh for early-stage, average ₹40 lakh up to ₹50 lakh for pilots or matched investment, up to ₹1 crore for select deep tech
eligibility: Technology startup, or an aspiring founder, student or researcher for the residence track
Focus on Tier-II and Tier-III cities
Selected through an implementing agency's expert process
Investment component needs 1:1 private sector matching
howToApply: Check the list of selected implementing agencies on MeitY Startup Hub
Apply to an agency near you or to the current EIR 3.0 call
Expect its own screening before any money is released
statusNote: Approved in July 2023 for five years. MeitY Startup Hub's September 2026 note says the EIR Cohort 3 call launched on 4 August 2026 is live. No closing date was shown. Other tracks run through implementing agencies.
watchOut: The ₹1 crore figure is only for a select few deep tech startups. Most founders see much smaller sums, the live call covers only the residence track, and implementing agencies decide. Check the closing date with MeitY Startup Hub.

name: Internet, Software and Cloud Reimbursement, Goa Startup Policy 2025
provider: Startup and IT Promotion Cell, Department of Information Technology, Government of Goa
summary: Goa startups working from their own or rented premises, not government facilities, can claim back internet connectivity, software licence and cloud service fees for one year. It suits software teams because it covers everyday running costs. The limit applies each quarter, and the policy also has a separate lease subsidy for local startups.
amount: Up to ₹1 lakh per quarter for one year
eligibility: Meets the Goa Startup Policy definition of a startup
Operates from own or rented premises, not a government facility
Costs are for internet, software licences or cloud services
Certified by the Startup and IT Promotion Cell

Claim through the single-window portal with bills
The cell assesses and the Empowered Committee sanctions
statusNote: Goa Startup Policy 2025 is linked on the portal and runs three years from gazette notification. The portal also shows an old notice about the 2017 policy. No claim dates seen.
watchOut: It lasts only one year, so time your claim to your highest spend. Confirm the 2025 policy schemes are live, because the portal still refers to older policies. The Goa portal's security certificate had expired when we checked, so your browser may show a warning.

name: Seed Capital Grant Scheme, Goa Startup Policy 2025
provider: Startup and IT Promotion Cell, Department of Information Technology, Government of Goa
summary: A one-time grant from the Goa government for startups that already have a promising minimum viable product. The state's startup cell decides the amount. A startup must be up to ten years old, with turnover up to ₹100 crore, and be incorporated or operating in Goa. Applications go through a single-window portal and a committee.
amount: Up to ₹10 lakh, as determined by the cell
eligibility: Registered or operating in Goa, up to ten years from incorporation
Annual turnover up to ₹100 crore
Private limited company, registered partnership or LLP
A promising minimum viable product
howToApply: Get certified as a startup by the Startup and IT Promotion Cell
Apply for incentives through the single-window portal
The cell assesses and the Empowered Committee sanctions
statusNote: Goa Startup Policy 2025 is linked on the portal and runs three years from gazette notification. The portal also shows an old notice about the 2017 policy and refers to 2021 schemes.
watchOut: The portal mixes old and new policy notices, so confirm that claims under the 2025 policy are open. The cell sets the amount, and only an MVP stage startup qualifies. The Goa portal's security certificate had expired when we checked, so your browser may show a warning.

name: Women Entrepreneur Vitality Scheme, Goa Startup Policy 2025
provider: Startup and IT Promotion Cell, Department of Information Technology, Government of Goa
summary: A monthly allowance for women-founded Goa startups at idea, prototype, validation or early traction stage, working in emerging technologies such as AI, IoT, drones, robotics, AR/VR and 3D printing. It is a one-time package lasting up to twelve months, with mentoring. Incubators or accelerators linked to the startup report progress every quarter.
amount: ₹20,000 a month for up to one year
eligibility: Startup founded by women
Meets the Goa Startup Policy definition of a startup
Works in an emerging technology such as AI, IoT, drones or AR/VR
Linked to an incubator or accelerator that can file quarterly reports
howToApply: Get certified by the Startup and IT Promotion Cell
Apply through the single-window portal
The cell does due diligence and approves it directly
statusNote: Goa Startup Policy 2025 is linked on the portal and runs three years from gazette notification. The portal also shows an old notice about the 2017 policy. No call dates seen.
watchOut: This is available only once and is modest money. Only emerging technology startups qualify, and you need a linked incubator or accelerator to report on your progress. The Goa portal's security certificate had expired when we checked, so your browser may show a warning.

name: Google for Startups Accelerator: India
provider: Google
summary: A three-month, equity-free programme for funded AI-first startups based in India, mainly at Seed to Series A. Selected teams get mentoring, training, expert access, early access to Google AI products and product credits. Cloud credits need a separate application. The page mentions no cash investment. Applications for the 2026 round have closed.
eligibility: Based or headquartered in India and funded, ideally Seed to Series A.
Past the idea stage, with customer validation and market traction.
Building AI-first products or foundational models with potential Google AI use cases.
Deeply technical, with a scalable product and a large market.
CEO, CTO and relevant team members must attend all programme elements.
howToApply: Applications are closed, so register interest for future programmes on the page.
When a new round opens, submit the application before the deadline.
Selection runs through eligibility review, a shortlist with interviews and pitches, then a final board.
statusNote: Applications for the 2026 round closed on 19 April 2026. That programme ran from June to September 2026. No next round is announced.
watchOut: Do not expect money. This is mentoring and access, with a selective funnel. It needs funding and traction, so an unfunded idea-stage founder will not fit.

name: Google for Startups Cloud Program
provider: Google Cloud
summary: Google Cloud credits matched to your stage. The Start tier gives up to $2,000 for young startups planning to raise venture money. The Scale tier gives up to $200,000 over two years to funded startups, or up to $350,000 for AI startups. Credits also cover Google models such as Gemini, plus training and support.
amount: Start tier up to $2,000 for one year. Scale tier up to $200,000 over two years, or up to $350,000 for AI startups.
eligibility: Start tier: founded in the last 24 months, with a working MVP, a clear business model and plans to seek venture funding soon.
Start tier: no Google Cloud credits received beyond the trial.
Scale tier: founded in the last five years, with Pre-Seed or Seed raised in the last five years, or Series A in the last 12 months.
Scale tier: no more than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits received so far.
Not open to agencies, consultancies, dev shops, nonprofits, educational institutions, government bodies, or companies that have listed or been acquired.
howToApply: Check your tier on the eligibility and benefits page.
Apply from the programme page, signed in with a Google account.
Google reviews the application against the listed requirements and matches you to a tier.
statusNote: Programme page and tier table live with no deadline shown. India is not named, and the tier rules show no country limit.
watchOut: The large amounts need verifiable funding. A bootstrapped founder gets at most $2,000, and only if founded within 24 months. Year 2 credits cover only 20% of usage, not all of it.

name: Student Startup and Innovation Policy (SSIP 2.0) Proof of Concept Support
provider: Education Department, Government of Gujarat
summary: Gujarat's student innovation policy pays for proof of concept and prototype work by people up to 35 years old who are students, alumni or dropouts of a Gujarat institution. Support reaches them through mapped universities and institutes, with up to ₹2.5 lakh per prototype for higher and technical education and help with patent costs.
amount: Up to ₹2.5 lakh per proof of concept or prototype, plus IP support up to 100% of expenses
eligibility: Age up to 35 years
Student, alumnus or alumna, or dropout
Registered as a beneficiary at a Gujarat educational institution
Innovation improves a product, process or service, or is a scalable business model
howToApply: Check whether your institution is a mapped grantee under SSIP
Register as a beneficiary at that institution
Submit your proposal for evaluation by the institution's committee
statusNote: Startup Gujarat page gives the policy period as January 11, 2022 to March 31, 2027, so the term is running. No central application window seen.
watchOut: This goes through your institute, so the bar and speed depend on them. Founders over 35 are out, and the policy term ends in March 2027 unless extended.

name: Startup Srujan Seed Support
provider: Student Startup and Innovation Hub (i-Hub), Education Department, Government of Gujarat
summary: A grant from Gujarat's i-Hub under SSIP 2.0 that helps young innovators and startups move from prototype to product and market. It is open to people up to 35 who are students, alumni or dropouts from Gujarat, at ideation, MVP or early stage. The amount depends on need, and it runs as cohorts.
amount: Between ₹2.5 lakh and ₹10 lakh, based on need
eligibility: Innovator or startup up to 35 years old
School or college student, alumnus or alumna, or dropout, from Gujarat
At ideation, validation (MVP) or early stage
howToApply: Read the S4 manual on the i-Hub site
Register and apply through the Srujan page while a cohort is open
A screening committee evaluates proposals
statusNote: i-Hub home page carries a notice inviting applications for Cohort 4, but the Srujan page still shows a last date of 31st May 2024. Current closing date could not be confirmed.
watchOut: Conflicting dates on the site mean you should email srujan@ihubgujarat.in before preparing. Founders over 35 are excluded, and the parent policy ends in March 2027 unless extended.

name: Reimbursement for Cloud Storage Scheme
provider: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Haryana
summary: Pays back part of what Startup Haryana registered startups spend on hosting and cloud computing, but only on data centres based in Haryana. Startups can claim 75% of the bill each year for five years. Pre-commercial startups get two years. Claims are made annually, with no carry forward between years.
amount: 75% of expenses, up to ₹2.5 lakh per startup per year
eligibility: Registered with Startup Haryana
Cloud services billed by a Haryana-based, tier certified data centre
Bills in the startup's name, paid from the company account
Applied within six months of the financial year end
howToApply: Register with Startup Haryana
Apply online each year with invoices, audited accounts and the data centre certificate
The department takes up to 30 working days on complete applications
statusNote: Scheme document says it runs till 06.07.2027 under the Haryana State Startup Policy 2022. Listed on the Startup Haryana schemes page with annual claims.
watchOut: Most small startups use AWS, GCP or Azure regions elsewhere, and those bills may not qualify. Check that your provider has a certified Haryana data centre before relying on this.

name: Seed Funding for Startups Scheme
provider: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Haryana
summary: A seed grant for DPIIT recognised startups registered in Haryana. It pays for validating an idea, proof of concept, prototype development, market research, marketing and some travel. The number of grants is capped by block category. Founders present to a committee that reviews applications each quarter.
amount: Up to ₹10 lakh per startup
eligibility: Category 1 startup registered with Startup Haryana
DPIIT recognised, with registered office in Haryana
Holds a Haryana Udhyam Memorandum
Not in the state's restricted list of activities
Has not taken similar incentives under another state policy

Apply online on the Industries and Commerce portal with the prescribed documents
Present your idea or product to the Evaluation and Approval Committee

watchOut: Office rent, team salaries, laptops and daily travel are all excluded. Travel and market research are capped at ₹50,000 each, so little remains unless you have real development or marketing costs.

name: Innovations for Defence Excellence
provider: Defence Innovation Organisation, Ministry of Defence
summary: Grant challenges that pay startups, MSMEs and individual innovators to build technology for the armed forces against published problem statements. Tracks include the Defence India Startup Challenge, the Open Challenge and iDEX Prime. Domains include AI, cryptography and communications as well as drones and radar. Winners can move towards procurement.
amount: Up to ₹1.5 crore under Defence India Startup Challenge, up to ₹10 crore under iDEX Prime
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup, or a company that is primarily an MSME
Individual innovators can also apply
Solution must answer a listed problem statement or qualify for the Open Challenge
howToApply: Watch the iDEX challenges page for a live edition
Read the problem statements and pick one you can solve
Apply online before the stated closing date
statusNote: Every listing on the challenges page showed closed. The latest were the Open Challenge on 30 September 2026, DISC 12 Re Open on 15 July 2026 and DISC 14 on 4 May 2026. No next edition is shown.

name: IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme

summary: Support for early-stage space startups and micro and small enterprises using space technology across upstream, midstream and downstream problems. Selected applicants get funding, mentoring, training and networking. IN-SPACe announces sector-specific opportunities from time to time, and looks for a clear business plan, target market and implementation strategy.

eligibility: Early-stage startup or micro or small enterprise
Innovative idea using space technology

A clear business plan and target market
